fun.signature: fun name(arg: Type) -> ReturnType { return value; }
fun.summary: Declare a function with typed parameters. Its return type may be written explicitly or inferred from return statements. Every path must return; functions capture surrounding bindings.
fun.example:
fun double(x: Int) -> Int { return x * 2 }
print(double(3));

let.signature: let name: Type = expression;  // Type may be inferred
let.summary: Declare an immutable binding. Mayc infers its type from the initializer when the annotation is omitted. Lists and maps stored in a let binding may still be mutated; their element types are checked.

mut.signature: mut name: Type = expression;  // Type may be inferred
mut.summary: Declare a mutable binding. Mayc infers its type from the initializer when the annotation is omitted. Later assignments must match that type.

if.summary: Evaluate a branch based on the condition. An `if` expression produces the chosen branch value.

else.summary: Provide the alternative branch of an `if` or `unless`. Chain `else if` for additional conditions.
else.example: let sign: Int = if (3 > 0) { 1 } else if (3 < 0) { -1 } else { 0 };

while.summary: Repeat a body while its condition is true. `break` stops the loop and `continue` skips to its next iteration.
while.example:
mut i: Int = 0;
while (i < 3) { print(i); i += 1; }

for.signature: for item in iterable { body }  // optional: item: Type
for.summary: Iterate over values or an integer range. Mayc infers the loop variable type from the iterable; an explicit type may be added as a checked constraint.
for.example:
for i: Int in 0..3 { print(i); }
let squares: List<Int> = [x * x for x: Int in [1, 2, 3]];

in.summary: Connect a loop or comprehension binding to its iterable. Range upper bounds use `..` for exclusive and `..=` for inclusive.
in.example: let evens: List<Int> = [x for x: Int in 0..6 if (x % 2 == 0)];

return.summary: Exit the enclosing function with a value of its declared return type. A bare return yields nil. Strict functions require explicit return on every path.

break.summary: Stop the innermost loop immediately. Execution resumes after the loop.
break.example: for x: Any in [1, 2, 3] { if (x == 2) { break; } print(x); }

continue.summary: Skip the remaining body of the innermost loop and advance to its next iteration.
continue.example: for x: Any in 0..4 { if (x == 2) { continue; } print(x); }

unless.summary: Execute the body when the condition is false. Useful for guard clauses; an `else` branch is also supported.
unless.example: fun head(xs: Any) -> Any { unless (len(xs) > 0) return nil; return xs[0] }

match.summary: Choose the first matching arm. Literal patterns, name bindings and the wildcard _ are supported by mayc.

may.summary: Catch a runtime failure within the block and evaluate a recovery expression. Inside `otherwise`, `err` contains the failure information.
may.example: let value: Any = may { int("oops") } otherwise { print(err.message); 0 };

otherwise.summary: Handle a failure from the preceding `may` block. `err.message` describes it and `err.kind` identifies its category.
otherwise.example: may { fail("missing item"); } otherwise { print(err.kind, err.message); };

struct.summary: Declare a record type with named fields. Construct values by calling the type name and access fields with `.`.

enum.summary: Declare tagged variants, optionally carrying values. Match variants to select behavior and bind their payloads.
enum.example:
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }
let color: Any = Red();

pub.summary: Export a top-level declaration from its module. When a module contains explicit public declarations, private declarations are hidden from importers.

extern.summary: Declare a foreign function for native linking. This requires an actual external symbol and suitable compiler/linker setup.

import.summary: Load a module relative to the current source file, then search the standard library. The `.may` suffix is optional. Use an alias for qualified access.

from.summary: Import selected public declarations into the current scope. Unselected names remain unavailable.

as.summary: Give an imported module a local namespace. Access its public declarations with `alias.name`.

and.summary: Evaluate logical conjunction with short circuiting. The right expression is skipped when the left expression is false.

or.summary: Evaluate logical disjunction with short circuiting. The right expression is skipped when the left expression is true.
or.example: let accepted: Any = true or false;

not.summary: Negate the truth value of an expression. `!` is the symbolic spelling.

true.summary: The boolean true value. Returned by successful comparisons and predicates.

false.summary: The boolean false value. Together with `nil`, it is false in condition tests.

nil.summary: Represent the absence of a value. Missing map lookups and empty `pop` calls produce `nil`; `??` supplies a fallback.

UInt8.summary: Unsigned 8 bit integer, also named Byte

Float32.summary: 32 bit floating point number, also named F32

Float64.summary: 64 bit floating point number, also named F64

Slice.summary: Borrowed view of a sequence with element type T

Tuple.summary: Tuple type containing the listed element types

Result.summary: Result type with success and error types

Array.summary: Fixed length array type with element type T

Never.summary: Type of an expression that cannot return normally

RawPtr.summary: Alias for Ptr, used for untyped native addresses

Int.summary: A signed 61-bit integer used for whole numbers, indexes, and system call arguments.

Str.summary: A UTF-8 string. Indexing and len use Unicode character positions.

Bool.summary: A boolean value, either true or false.

List.summary: An ordered mutable collection whose elements have type T.

Map.summary: A mutable key-value collection with key type K and value type V.

Any.summary: A dynamic value that can hold any runtime type.

Nil.summary: The type of the absence value nil.

Ptr.summary: A raw memory address used by native operations and syscalls.

Optional.summary: A value of type T or nil.

??.summary: Return the fallback only when the left value is `nil`. Values such as `0` and `false` are preserved.

?..summary: Access a field only if the receiver is present. A `nil` receiver yields `nil` instead of a field access failure.

|>.summary: Pass the left value as the first argument of the function on the right. Pipelines can be chained.
|>.example: print([1, 2, 3] |> map(|x: Any| -> Any { return x * 2; }) |> sum);

...summary: An integer range with an exclusive upper endpoint, suitable for loops and comprehensions.

..=.summary: An integer range that includes its upper endpoint.

=>.summary: Separate a match pattern from its result. Legacy code also uses this for short lambdas; strict lambdas require typed parameters, a return type and an explicit return.

->.summary: Declare the required return type of a named or anonymous function. Use explicit return statements in its body.

**.summary: Raise a number to a power. Integer and floating-point operands are supported by the native runtime.

print.summary: Write values to standard output, separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
print.returns: Used for its output side effect; the native runtime currently produces zero.

parameters.name: values...
parameters.description: Values to display, converted using runtime formatting.

len.summary: Count list elements, map entries, or Unicode characters in a string.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The string, list, or map to measure.

str.summary: Convert a value to its textual representation.

int.summary: Convert an integer, float, or decimal string to an integer. Floats are truncated toward zero; invalid text raises a catchable failure.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A number or a trimmed decimal string with optional sign.

float.summary: Convert a number or numeric string to a floating-point value.

to_float.summary: Convert a value using the native floating-point conversion helper.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The numeric value or string to convert.

bool.summary: Convert a value to its truth value. Only `nil` and `false` are false; zero, empty strings, and empty collections are true.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value whose truthiness is tested.

push.summary: Append one item to the existing list. All aliases of that list observe the mutation.

pop.summary: Remove and return the last item of the existing list.
pop.returns: The removed item, or `nil` when empty.

map.summary: Call a function once for each list item and collect the returned values. The input list is preserved.
map.returns: A new list of transformed values.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: A function taking one item and returning its replacement.

filter.summary: Collect input items for which the predicate returns the boolean `true`.
filter.returns: A new list containing matching items.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: A function taking one item and returning a boolean.

reduce.summary: Fold a list from left to right, passing the accumulator and current item to the function.
reduce.example: print(reduce([1, 2, 3], |acc: Any, x: Any| -> Any { return acc + x; }, 0));
reduce.returns: The final accumulator, or `init` for an empty list.

sum.summary: Add the numeric values in a list.
sum.returns: The total; zero for an empty list.

any.summary: Test whether at least one item makes the predicate return `true`. Stop at the first match.
any.returns: A boolean; `false` for an empty list.

all.summary: Test whether every item makes the predicate return `true`. Stop at the first nonmatching item.
all.returns: A boolean; `true` for an empty list.

min.summary: Return the lesser of two comparable values.

max.summary: Return the greater of two comparable values.

abs.summary: Return the nonnegative magnitude of a number.

sort.summary: Return the items in ascending order using the standard comparison function. The input list is preserved.

reverse.summary: Build a list with the input items in reverse order.

slice.summary: Copy a contiguous section of a list. Bounds are clamped to the list length; the stop index is exclusive.
slice.returns: A new list; empty if stop is not greater than start.

keys.summary: Collect the keys of a map.

values.summary: Collect the values of a map.

has.summary: Check for a map key, a matching list item, or a substring within a string.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The map, list, or string to search.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key, item, or substring to find.

map_get.summary: Look up a map entry without changing the map.
map_get.returns: The stored value, or `nil` if missing.

map_set.summary: Insert or replace an entry in the existing map.

remove.summary: Copy a map while omitting one key. The original map is preserved.
remove.example:
let m: Any = {"a": 1, "b": 2};
let smaller: Any = remove(m, "a");

merge.summary: Combine two maps into a new map. Entries from the second map replace matching keys from the first.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: The second map, which takes precedence.

read_file.summary: Read a file into a string. An I/O failure can be caught with `may` / `otherwise`.
read_file.example: let text: Any = may { read_file("notes.txt") } otherwise { "" };
read_file.returns: The file contents as a string.

write_file.summary: Write a string to a file, creating it or replacing its existing contents. I/O failures are catchable.

read_dir.summary: List names in a directory, excluding `.` and `..`. Names are relative to the supplied directory.
read_dir.returns: A list of names; empty if the directory cannot be read.

file_exists.summary: Test whether a filesystem path exists.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file or directory path to test.

json_parse.summary: Decode a JSON string into Maylang strings, numbers, booleans, lists, maps, and `nil`.

json_stringify.summary: Encode a value as JSON text. Strings are quoted and escaped; lists and maps are encoded recursively.

input.summary: Display a prompt and read one line from standard input. The trailing newline is removed.
input.returns: A string, or `nil` at end of input.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: The text to display before reading; `nil` suppresses it.

read_stdin.summary: Read standard input until end of file. This waits for EOF, so it is suitable for piped data.
read_stdin.returns: The collected input as a string.

clock.summary: Read the wall clock as fractional seconds since the Unix epoch.
clock.example:
let before: Any = clock();
print(clock() - before);
clock.notes: This is a wall clock, so clock adjustments can change elapsed-time measurements.

time.summary: Read the current Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

sleep.summary: Pause the calling thread for a duration measured in milliseconds.

spawn.summary: Register a zero-argument function as a cooperative fiber. Call `run()` to execute scheduled fibers.

yield.summary: Suspend the current cooperative fiber so another scheduled fiber can run. Outside a fiber it has no scheduling effect.
yield.example:
spawn(fun() -> Any { print("first"); yield(); return print("again"); });
run();

run.summary: Execute scheduled cooperative fibers until they finish. Fibers yield explicitly with `yield()`.

fail.summary: Raise a runtime failure. A surrounding `may` block can catch it and access `err.message`.

exit.summary: Terminate the process with an exit status. Zero conventionally indicates success.

syscall.summary: Invoke a Linux system call directly, with up to six integer arguments. This bypasses normal file and memory helpers.
syscall.example: let pid: Any = syscall(39); // Linux getpid
syscall.returns: The raw integer result; failures usually return a negative errno.

parameters.name: arguments...
parameters.description: Raw integer arguments in syscall order.

addr.summary: Return the address of a string’s UTF-8 bytes. Keep the string alive while using the address.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: The string whose byte storage is addressed.

cstr.summary: Create a NUL-terminated representation of a string for a native API.
cstr.returns: An integer address to NUL-terminated bytes.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: The string to pass to native code.

load8.summary: Read 8 bits from a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
load8.example:
let s: Any = "abcdefgh";
let value: Any = load8(addr(s));

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid readable address with enough remaining bytes.

store8.summary: Write 8 bits to a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
store8.example:
// p must refer to writable allocated memory.
store8(p, 0);

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid writable address with enough remaining bytes.

load16.summary: Read 16 bits from a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
load16.example:
let s: Any = "abcdefgh";
let value: Any = load16(addr(s));

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid readable address with enough remaining bytes.

store16.summary: Write 16 bits to a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
store16.example:
// p must refer to writable allocated memory.
store16(p, 0);

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid writable address with enough remaining bytes.

load32.summary: Read 32 bits from a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
load32.example:
let s: Any = "abcdefgh";
let value: Any = load32(addr(s));

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid readable address with enough remaining bytes.

store32.summary: Write 32 bits to a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
store32.example:
// p must refer to writable allocated memory.
store32(p, 0);

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid writable address with enough remaining bytes.

load64.summary: Read 64 bits from a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
load64.example:
let s: Any = "abcdefgh";
let value: Any = load64(addr(s));

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid readable address with enough remaining bytes.

store64.summary: Write 64 bits to a raw memory address. This operation performs no bounds or lifetime checks.
store64.example:
// p must refer to writable allocated memory.
store64(p, 0);

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: A valid writable address with enough remaining bytes.

ccall.summary: Call machine code at a raw address with up to six integer arguments using the native calling convention.
ccall.example:
// fn must be a valid native function address.
let result: Any = ccall(fn, [1, 2]);

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: A list of at most six integer arguments.

extern_c.summary: Wrap a native function address as a callable Maylang function accepting six integer arguments.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The number to evaluate; trigonometric angles use radians.

floor.summary: Round a number down to an integer-valued numeric result.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The number to evaluate; trigonometric angles use radians.

ceil.summary: Round a number up to an integer-valued numeric result.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The number to evaluate; trigonometric angles use radians.

sin.summary: Compute the sine of an angle in radians.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The number to evaluate; trigonometric angles use radians.

cos.summary: Compute the cosine of an angle in radians.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The number to evaluate; trigonometric angles use radians.

tan.summary: Compute the tangent of an angle in radians.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The number to evaluate; trigonometric angles use radians.

env.summary: Look up an environment variable in the current process.
env.returns: The variable’s string value, or `nil` if missing.

args.summary: Read the process’s command-line arguments, including the executable name as the first item.

substring.summary: Copy a section of a string using Unicode character indices. The third argument is a count, not an ending index.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of characters to copy.

split.summary: Separate a string at occurrences of a separator.

join.summary: Convert items to strings and combine them with a separator between neighboring items.

trim.summary: Remove whitespace from the beginning and end of a string.

range.summary: Build a list of consecutive integers from the start up to, but excluding, the stop value.

err.summary: The error object available inside an `otherwise` recovery block.
